nodes.name: Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API)
nodes.definition: The chemically defined biological entity responsible for physiological alteration, therapeutic efficacy, or diagnostic utility in a pharmaceutical dosage form.

nodes.name: Ferguson Principle
nodes.definition: A thermodynamic law stating that the biological potency of structurally non-specific drugs is governed by their relative saturation in the biophase rather than chemical binding specificity.

nodes.name: Structurally Specific Drugs
nodes.definition: Therapeutic agents whose biological response depends upon exact 3D spatial complementarity, electrostatic interaction, and stereochemical fit with a targeted macromolecular receptor or enzyme active site.

nodes.name: Structurally Non-Specific Drugs
nodes.definition: Molecules that elicit pharmacologic action primarily through collective physicochemical perturbations (such as membrane fluidization or vapor pressure accumulation) without high-affinity receptor binding.

nodes.name: Aqueous Solubility & Dissolution
nodes.definition: The thermodynamic equilibrium concentration of a solute dissolved in water, fundamentally limiting drug dissolution rate and systemic gastrointestinal absorption.

nodes.name: Partition Coefficient (P and log P)
nodes.definition: The ratio of unionized drug concentrations distributed between an organic lipid phase (1-octanol) and an aqueous phase at thermodynamic equilibrium, quantifying lipophilicity.

nodes.name: Hansch Substituent Constant (pi)
nodes.definition: A linear free-energy parameter measuring the differential lipophilic contribution of a chemical substituent relative to hydrogen on an aromatic or aliphatic scaffold.

nodes.name: Lipinski's Rule of Five
nodes.definition: A set of four physicochemical cutoff heuristics (MW <= 500, log P <= 5, HBD <= 5, HBA <= 10) predictive of poor oral absorption or membrane permeability.

nodes.name: Functional Group Ionization & pKa
nodes.definition: The quantitative acid dissociation constant determining the equilibrium fraction of ionized versus neutral drug species across gastrointestinal and physiological pH environments.

nodes.name: Amine Protonation & Pharmacophore Binding
nodes.definition: The ability of primary, secondary, and tertiary amines to undergo protonation at physiological pH 7.4, enabling essential electrostatic bonds with anionic receptor carboxylates.

nodes.name: Carboxylic Acid Functional Group
nodes.definition: An acidic pharmacophoric moiety (pKa 3-5) that exists primarily as an anion at pH 7.4, forming ionic contacts or undergoing Phase II acyl glucuronidation.

nodes.name: Heterocyclic Drug Scaffolds
nodes.definition: Aromatic or saturated ring systems containing nitrogen, oxygen, or sulfur that rigidify pharmacophore geometry and serve as hydrogen bond donors or acceptors.

nodes.name: Geometric (Cis/Trans, E/Z) Isomerism
nodes.definition: Diastereomeric configuration resulting from restricted rotation about double bonds or cycloalkanes, causing distinct interatomic distances between pharmacophore groups.

nodes.name: Optical Isomerism & Enantiomers
nodes.definition: Molecules bearing chiral centers lacking internal symmetry planes that form non-superimposable mirror images exhibiting identical physical constants but opposite optical rotation.

nodes.name: Easson-Stedman Three-Point Attachment Model
nodes.definition: The biological stereoselectivity hypothesis stating that high-affinity receptor activation requires minimum three simultaneous, complementary spatial contacts between ligand and binding pocket.

nodes.name: Eutomer, Distomer & Eudismic Ratio
nodes.definition: The therapeutic classification of the higher-affinity active enantiomer (eutomer) versus the lower-affinity/inactive/toxic antipode (distomer), whose affinity ratio represents the eudismic ratio.

nodes.name: Thalidomide Stereochemical Toxicity Case
nodes.definition: A historical case demonstrating that while (R)-thalidomide exerts hypnotic efficacy, (S)-thalidomide causes severe teratogenic phocomelia, complicated by rapid in vivo metabolic racemization.

nodes.name: Conformational Isomerism & Dynamic Receptor Selection
nodes.definition: Interconvertible spatial arrangements generated by rotation around single sigma bonds, allowing flexible endogenous transmitters (acetylcholine, histamine) to selectively activate distinct receptor subtypes.

nodes.name: Classical Bioisosterism
nodes.definition: Structural replacement using atoms or groups sharing identical outer electronic configurations and valence electrons (Grimm hydride displacement and Erlenmeyer rules) to maintain biological activity.

nodes.name: Non-Classical Bioisosterism
nodes.definition: Substitutions of groups with differing electronic topologies and atom counts that produce analogous biological outcomes by mimicking spatial geometry, electronic density, or pKa (e.g. tetrazole for carboxylate).

nodes.name: Tetrazole-Carboxylate Bioisosteric Replacement
nodes.definition: Replacement of an ionizable carboxylic acid group with a planar, lipophilic 1H-tetrazole ring (pKa ~4.5-4.9), markedly enhancing oral bioavailability and metabolic stability against glucuronidation.

nodes.name: Phase I CYP450 Functionalization Oxidation
nodes.definition: Hepatic microsomal mixed-function oxidase catalytic reactions that introduce or unmask reactive polar functional groups (-OH, -NH2, -SH) via cytochrome P450 enzymes.

nodes.name: Aromatic Hydroxylation & Arene Oxide Intermediates
nodes.definition: Electrophilic oxidation of aromatic drug rings generating transient, reactive arene oxides that either isomerize to phenols via NIH shift, hydrate via epoxide hydrolase, or conjugate with glutathione.

nodes.name: Phase II Glucuronic Acid Conjugation
nodes.definition: The principal human conjugation pathway mediated by UDP-glucuronosyltransferases (UGT), transferring glucuronic acid from UDPGA to nucleophilic oxygens, nitrogens, or sulfurs to generate excretable hydrophilic glucuronides.

nodes.name: N-Acetylation & Genetic Polymorphism
nodes.definition: Phase II transfer of an acetyl moiety from Acetyl-CoA to primary aromatic amines via NAT2, exhibiting trimodal human genetic polymorphism that stratifies patients into rapid and slow acetylator phenotypes.

nodes.name: Glutathione Conjugation & Mercapturic Acid Pathway
nodes.definition: Protective nucleophilic scavenging of electrophilic toxic drug metabolites (e.g. NAPQI) by the cellular tripeptide glutathione (GSH) via GST, subsequently processed into urinary mercapturic acids.
